Today we're deciding: Choose a format for a student hackathon project showcase.
For this simulated decision, I’ll treat the following setup as the shared facts.
Options:
A) Rotating Demo Stations with Timed Slots — duration per team: 10 minutes; audience capacity: small groups of 5-7; interaction level: high (+ Allows close interaction and detailed demos with each team; − Limited audience size per slot may reduce overall exposure)
B) Central Stage Presentation with Q&A — duration per team: 7 minutes; audience capacity: up to 100 people; interaction level: moderate (+ Maximizes audience size and formal presentation experience; − Less opportunity for hands-on interaction with projects)
C) Virtual Showcase via Live Streaming Platform — duration per team: 5 minutes pre-recorded plus 5 minutes live Q&A; audience capacity: unlimited online viewers; interaction level: moderate (+ Enables broad remote participation and flexible viewing; − Technical issues may disrupt flow and reduce engagement)
D) Poster Session with Walkaround Networking — duration per team: entire 3-hour event; audience capacity: varies, walk-in style; interaction level: high (+ Encourages informal conversations and networking throughout the event; − Risk of uneven attention as audience may not visit all teams)
Context: The student hackathon project showcase will feature 15 teams presenting their work.; The decision group consists of exactly 7 participants responsible for choosing the format.; The showcase must fit within a 3-hour time window on a single day.
Let's discuss which option fits best overall.
